facts.text: Eads was founded in 1887 as a railroad town and named after engineer James Buchanan Eads who built the famous Eads Bridge over the Mississippi.
The town’s historic downtown is being revitalized through a partnership that includes the National Park Service and the Colorado Historical Society.
The Sand Creek Massacre National Historic Site, a key reminder of the 1864 tragedy, sits just outside Eads and is a National Historic Site.
Eads became the county seat of Kiowa County in 1902, making it the administrative center of the region.
The annual Maine Street Bash, started in 2007, brings local businesses together for live performances and community celebration.
The Bransgrove Building, the first historic structure rehabilitated in Eads, now houses offices and retail space, showcasing adaptive reuse.
